reason: The tweet’s widgets script: React hoists it into the head, and Astro leaves it inline where the post has it
next/script injects the Twitter widget from the client, and Astro writes the tag; both preload it in the head
src/scripts/copy-code.js finds code figures’ copy buttons by data-copy-code, where React gave each button its own handler
The build reads the subscriber count from EmailOctopus once per build. Production’s count API call fails, so it always shows the 700 fallback
The GitHub link names the content file, now .mdx
Next to read picks two posts at random each time the page renders
next/image’s blur placeholder. Every use passes the same transparent 1×1 GIF, so it never showed anything, and the build leaves it out
React 19 preloads the first images it renders without loading=lazy, here a plain markdown image further down the post
Production’s home canonical and og:url point at /index, which 308s to / (since #369). The build points at the root
The 404 gets the full layout head, a single noindex, and no canonical or og:url. Production’s has both robots values and a canonical to the missing URL
The paged category route matches slugs the way the category page does. Production capitalises the slug, so these 404
View counts are read when each side renders, so they drift between the snapshot and the build
Production renders the home page as /index, so its tab isn’t marked current. The build marks it
React Aria’s Select renders a hidden native select and a template for its popover. They arrive with the popular posts island
Production’s 404 sends an empty body and draws the page from the RSC payload once JavaScript runs. The build sends the page itself
Campaigns: production fetches /api/campaigns after load, so its HTML only has “Loading...”. The build reads the issues from EmailOctopus once per build and lists them

Production lists these posts in the shared allPosts array’s order, which another page’s in-place sort may have changed first in the same server process, so it flips between file order and newest first. The build always lists them newest first
New: the home page’s markdown at its own URL, where Accept negotiation for / will point. Production only rewrote / with that Accept header
Until phase 4: these files have no extension, so their Content-Type comes from vercel.json, which doesn’t exist yet
Fixed: views are looked up by the bare slug the table keys them on. Production looks them up by the /blog/ path, which never matches, so its most viewed posts are really the oldest in file order
Fixed: the markdown of draft and closed posts isn’t served, as their pages aren’t. Production serves it
